title: World Outliner & Details Panel 📋
description: Control every actor in your scene and edit properties precisely.

slides.title: World Outliner: The Actor List 📜
slides.content:
# Your Scene’s Inventory

The World Outliner shows every actor currently placed in your level. Think of it as a **spreadsheet of objects**.

* **Name** – click to rename.
* **Eye icon** – toggle visibility.
* **Lock icon** – prevent selection/movement.
* **Folder icon** – organise actors into folders (vital for large levels).
* **Search bar** – filter by name or type.
* **Type column** – shows actor class (Static Mesh Actor, Light, etc.).

Right‑click an actor to access: Edit, Delete, Find in Content Browser, Attach To, Create Child Blueprint.

quizData.question: You can organise actors into folders inside the World Outliner to keep your level tidy.
quizData.explanation: Use the Create Folder button or right‑click to group actors. Folders only affect the Outliner, not the 3D hierarchy.

slides.title: Selection & Hierarchy 🔗
slides.content:
## Parent‑Child Relationships

Actors can be parented to each other:
* Drag actor A onto actor B in the Outliner → A becomes a child of B.
* Moving/rotating/scaling the parent affects all children.
* Useful for grouping props, attaching lights to a ceiling, etc.

Use the **Attach To** right‑click command to quickly set parents without dragging.

slides.title: Details Panel Deep Dive 📝
slides.content:
## Every Setting Imaginable

Select an actor and the Details Panel reveals:

* **Transform** – Location, Rotation, Scale (absolute and relative).
* **Actor** – general settings: Mobility, Tags, Can be Damaged.
* **Component‑specific sections** – e.g., Static Mesh, Collision, Materials.
* **Search bar** at the top – instantly find a property (type `cast shadow`).

**Blue values** mean the property is set to the class default. **Yellow values** mean you’ve overridden it. This colour coding helps you track changes.

quizData.question: In the Details Panel, what does a yellow‑coloured property value indicate?

options.text: It has been overridden from the default

quizData.explanation: Yellow indicates the property has been changed from the class default. Blue is the default.

slides.title: Multi‑Selection & Bulk Edit ✨
slides.content:
## Edit Many at Once

Hold **Ctrl** and click multiple actors in the Outliner or viewport. The Details Panel now shows **only properties common** to all selected actors.

* Change a value and it applies to all selected actors instantly.
* Great for moving/rotating groups or adjusting shared material properties.

Use **Shift** click for range selection.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Lock the Details Panel

Click the **lock icon** (top‑right of Details Panel) to freeze the current actor’s properties. Now you can select other actors for reference while still editing the locked one. Unlock when done.
